registers.role: sample frame, linkage, treatment inputs (income and number of children), outcomes and controls
variables_mentioned: labor market behavior (employment, labor force status, and annual wages)
residence address (one per individual per year)

registers.name_in_paper: tax-deductible annual child support payments reported to the tax authorities
registers.role: outcomes: fathers' child support payments (all payments above the non-tax-deductible extra amount)

registers.name_in_paper: the State Administration's (Statsforvaltningen) annual government-mandated child support formula
registers.role: treatment construction: the simulated child support obligation (Online Appendix Table A1 shows the scheme for 1999, 2005 and 2008)
variables_mentioned: income thresholds by number of children

registers.name_in_paper: Danish longitudinal survey of children (DALSC), 1999 wave
registers.role: supplementary descriptive evidence on physical custody arrangements and in-kind transfers (380 families; Online Appendix B)

linkages: children are linked to their parents regardless of residence status
fathers are linked to their oldest children's mothers (40,109 father-mother pairs; 39,550 unique mothers)
the administrative data are linked to survey data with parent-reported information on custody arrangements (Online Appendix B)

sample.universe: all children born in Denmark over 1985-2010, their siblings and their parents
sample.unit_of_observation: father (the analysis is cross-sectional and uses one observation per father); mother for maternal outcomes; cells of 15,000 DKK father income bin x number of children x year for Table 1
selection_rules: begin with all fathers observed in the register data in every year from 1998 to 2013

keep fathers who were either (i) married to or cohabiting with their first children's mothers in the year of childbirth (or in 1998 for first children born before), or (ii) had a first child between 1999 and 2010 while not married to nor cohabiting with the child's mother
define the father's separation year as the year in which he either no longer resides with his oldest child's mother or has a first child while not living with the child's mother
limit to the 137,715 fathers with separation years between 1999 and 2010 (2010 is chosen so that at least three post-separation years are observed)
keep only fathers who had at most two children aged less than 18 at separation (the roughly 10% with more children are dropped)
keep only fathers with separation year annual incomes within 270,000-405,000 DKK in real year 2000 terms, giving 40,109 fathers linked to their children and their children's mothers
for maternal outcomes, use the 39,550 unique mothers linked to these fathers, focusing on the first separation spell observed in the data

for Table 1, start instead from the full panel of parents (including those who always stay together), keep father-year observations only until the year of separation, apply the same income, number-of-children and observation-window restrictions, and collapse the data into 260 cells
sample.n_observations: 40,109 fathers (39,550 mothers for maternal outcomes; 260 cells in Table 1)

construction_notes: the child support obligation is computed for every father from the State Administration's formula, a step function of his gross income whose amounts and thresholds change every year and vary with his number of biological children under age 18, including children from new unions

AvgOblig_itk = (1/(T+1)) sum_{j=0}^{T} g_{t+j}(I_{i,t+j}, K_{k,t+j}) is the average annual obligation over all observed post-separation years; SepOblig_itk = g_{t,k}(I_{i,t}) is the simulated obligation using separation-year income and number of children only
all obligations, payments and incomes are expressed in real year 2000 DKK in units of 1000 DKK, so coefficients are per 1000 DKK

observed payments are tax-deductible payments reported to the tax authorities, i.e. payments above the non-tax-deductible extra amount; the average annual obligation net of the extra amount is 18,850 DKK against an average annual payment net of the extra amount of 9957 DKK
real average annual obligations range between 896 DKK and 65,532 DKK (0.3-20% of fathers' annual gross incomes); the median real average annual obligation is 20,546 DKK

fathers pay about 55% of their tax-deductible obligation; 16% of sample fathers make zero payments post-separation, 76% pay more than zero but less than the obligation and 9% pay the obligation or more; among those paying a strictly positive amount the average is 65% of the obligation

father-child co-residence is measured from the single registered residence address per individual per year, so the measure includes joint and sole-father physical custody but underestimates joint custody

the control function f(I_it) is specified as indicators for 15,000 DKK (approximately $2410) annual income bins of the father's real separation year income; robustness uses linear, quadratic, cubic and quartic polynomials

Table 1 regressions are weighted by the number of observations in each cell, with robust standard errors clustered on the cell level; all other regressions use standard errors robust to heteroskedasticity
average separation year real gross incomes are 323,700 DKK for fathers and 221,000 DKK for mothers, against 299,500 DKK and 198,500 DKK for all Danish fathers and mothers in this period

claims.statement: The anticipated child support obligation has no statistically significant effect on the share of parents who divorce, separate, or have an out-of-wedlock/cohabitation birth in a year.

treatment.label: Child support obligation (anticipated), in year 2000 real units of 1000 DKK

definition.value: The government-mandated child support obligation implied by the Danish child support formula for the cell's father income bin, number of children (one or two) and year, assigned to father-year observations up to and including the year of separation; the paper calls it the anticipated paternal child support obligation. Expressed in year 2000 real units of 1000 DKK.

timing.value: Measured in each father-year observation before and including the year of separation (i.e. before the separation decision is made).

identification.source_of_variation: formula-driven variation in the government-mandated child support obligation across 15,000 DKK father income bins, number of children (one or two) and year, with main effects and double interactions absorbed (a 'triple-difference' model), estimated on 260 cells

key_assumptions.supported_by: the same conditioning set the paper states as its identifying assumption for Eqs. (3) and (4)

key_assumptions.assumption: The cell-level regression, weighted by the number of observations in each cell and linear in the obligation, recovers the relationship between the obligation and the probability that parents separate.

definition.value: The father's government-mandated child support obligation, computed from the Danish child support formula g(.)_{t+j} (a step function of the father's gross income that changes every year and varies with his number of biological children under age 18), evaluated in each year observed post-separation and averaged over those years: AvgOblig_itk = (1/(T+1)) sum_{j=0}^{T} g_{t+j}(I_{i,t+j}, K_{k,t+j}).
